subject: Renewal: Q4 seasonal-burst buffer and right-sizing for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Li <evan@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Q4 seasonal-burst buffer and right-sizing for Dedicated capacity

Evan —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is a first pass at a renewal framework that reflects BlueHarbor's trailing 6-month usage pattern (see attached usage_summary_2026H2.csv). High level: your baseline commit (currently 80 GPUs) has been underutilized most weekdays but spikes during heavy model-training windows and Q4 batch re-runs. To balance predictability and cost, we propose the following: 

- Baseline commit: 72 GPUs (monthly guaranteed capacity)
- Q4 seasonal-burst buffer: +12 GPUs reserved as a "burst pool" available on-demand for short windows (per-hour billing for burst beyond baseline)
- Auto-scale trigger: sustained 75% baseline utilization across a rolling 7-day window will activate a temporary tranche increase (up to +20 GPUs) for up to 72 hours
- Reporting & credits: any sustained underutilization (<50% baseline for 30 consecutive days) will be eligible for a one-time credit conversation at renewal

Why this helps: reduces committed spend when your baseline is idle, preserves headroom for predictable seasonal spikes, and gives you a documented auto-scale behavior to avoid failed requests during bursts.

Next steps: if this approach looks reasonable, I can circulate a clean amendment (redwood_proposal_amendment_v2.pdf) and cost delta table. Dev, Marissa — please flag any technical or billing caveats. Evan — can we aim for a short call next week to lock terms?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: RE: Renewal: Q4 seasonal-burst buffer and right-sizing for Dedicated capacity

Ben / Marissa —

Quick technical + billing notes for Evan's questions: 

- Burst pool semantics: recommend treating the 12-GPU burst pool as metered "soft reserve" — it is guaranteed to be available for pre-approved burst windows but billed at a reduced overage rate (e.g., 0.65x of spot rate) rather than counting toward the committed GPU discount tiers. This preserves your commit-level pricing while keeping cost visible.

- Auto-scale billing example (approx): baseline 72 GPUs = $X/day. If baseline utilization triggers and +15 GPUs run for 72 hours, billing shows: baseline commit billed at committed rate; +15 GPUs billed at burst overage rate on a per-second basis. Estimated incremental cost for that 3-day event: ~8–12% of monthly baseline, depending on sequence length and batching. I'll attach a sample cost calc to the proposal.

- Implementation notes: we can enforce the 7-day rolling trigger in the routing layer and the orchestration plane will activate a pre-warmed pool. We'll also enable KV-prefix caching cutoffs to avoid reloading large KV segments when burst opens. No model retrains required.

- Telemetry: add two metrics to monitor pre-renewal — 1) 95th-percentile concurrent GPU usage, 2) median sequence length during spike windows. These will feed the canary that flips the temporary tranche.

Cheers,
Dev
Dev Patel

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:45:10 -0700
Subject: Revised proposal and price summary (attached)

Evan / Team —

Attached is the revised amendment (redwood_proposal_amendment_v2.pdf) that incorporates Dev's notes and a concise price table. Key bullets from the attachment: 

- Baseline: 72 GPUs @ committed rate $/GPU/mo
- Burst pool: 12 GPUs billed at "burst rate" (metered per-second; capped daily) — does not count toward tiered commit discounts
- Auto-scale: additional temporary tranche up to +20 GPUs; triggered by 7-day rolling utilization >75%; capped at 72 hours per event
- Estimated expected delta (based on 6-months): +9% month-over-month cost in heavy months, ~-6% in light months vs current 80-GPU flat commit

If procurement is comfortable, we can move to DocuSign and a 60-day pilot that starts Nov 15 to cover the Q4 seasonality. Attached files: redwood_proposal_amendment_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB), usage_summary_2026H2.csv (CSV, 86KB).

Ben
